profit_quality.assessment: Accounting profit is stable, but cash conversion is poor because receivables, contract assets, inventories and restricted deposits absorb cash in a project-based rail transit systems business.
adjustments: Used recent stable parent net profit and operating profit as the starting point, but did not treat full accounting profit as distributable cash.
Deducted estimated maintenance capex of HK$45m based on recent PPE/intangible purchase cash outflows.
Deducted HK$20m normal working-capital reinvestment and then applied a 0.35 profit haircut because 2022-2024 median post-capex free cash flow was negative.
Share of JV/associate results and fair-value changes are not given full cash value in the distributable-profit denominator.
profit_quality.cashflow_support: 2024 CFO was HK$227.864m, but 2023 CFO was HK$8.685m and 2022 CFO was negative HK$155.183m; post-capex FCF was HK$180.629m, negative HK$36.010m and negative HK$194.759m respectively.
profit_quality.haircut_reason: 0.35 is in the low end for profits that repeatedly convert into receivables/contract assets and require ongoing project working capital.
profit_quality.cash_conversion_assessment: Three-year median CFO / median parent profit is about 5.0%; median free cash flow after capex is negative.
profit_quality.maintenance_capex_assessment: No exact maintenance capex split; HK$45m approximates recent annual PPE/intangible purchase cash outflows.
profit_quality.working_capital_assessment: Large trade receivables, bills receivable and contract assets make cash extraction uncertain; retention periods can run one to three years.
